title: SLI Declaration and Regional Fallback Band Policy (per-endpoint/model)
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
This ticket captures a canonical SLI/SLO declaration for per-endpoint and per-model routes, plus a deterministic policy for regional fallback bands and circuit-breaker thresholds used during overloads or regional outages. Goal: give on-call and routing systems a compact, auditable contract to drive automated failover, load-shedding and throttling decisions without ad-hoc heuristics.

Scope:
- All externally-visible model routes (text-generation chat, embeddings, rerank) and internal backend routes used by Dedicated/Private control plane.
- Per-route SLIs (latency percentiles, availability, correctness where applicable).
- Error budget burn rate mapping -> automated actions (soft throttle, shard eviction, regional ejection).
- Regional fallback "bands": ordered sets of compatible model variants + capacity slices for graceful degradation.
- Circuit-breaker thresholds tied to SLI burn rate and queue length signals.

Definitions and rationale:
- SLI types we standardize on:
  - Latency P50 / P95 / P99 (ms) for request-to-first-token and request-to-last-token where applicable.
  - Availability: successful-response-rate (2xx or 3xx) measured at the model route level.
  - Quality SLI (optional per-model): rouge-like eval pass-rate over daily promptset (used for rollback gating, not automated failover).

Per-endpoint SLI declarations (examples):
- /v1/generate (chat, default model):
  - availability: >= 99.9% monthly SLO, SLI = successful_responses / total_requests (exclude client-initiated cancellations).
  - latency: P95(first_token) < 300ms, P99(first_token) < 800ms.
  - quality: eval-pass-rate >= 98% (measured daily on stable promptset; used for rollout safety).
- /v1/embeddings (embed-large):
  - availability: >= 99.95% monthly.
  - latency: P95 < 120ms, P99 < 350ms.
- /internal/controlplane/deploy (control plane):
  - availability: >= 99.99% monthly (higher SLA).
  - latency P95 < 500ms.

Measurement and instrumentation (concrete queries):
- Source of truth: metrics-prod (Prometheus/Thanos). We publish derived SLIs to the SLO service for burn analysis.
- Availability SLI (PromQL example):
  - success_rate = (sum(rate(http_requests_total{route="/v1/generate",status=~"2..|3.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{route="/v1/generate"}[5m])))
- Latency SLI (P99 first token): use histogram_quantile over request_first_token_latency_seconds_bucket by route/model/version.

Error budget policy and automated actions:
- Error budget: 1 - SLO (e.g., 0.1% monthly). We treat burn-rate windows as short (1h), medium (6h), long (72h).
- Burn-rate triggers -> actions:
  - burn_rate > 3x for 1h: create pager (severity P0), initiate soft throttle (5% global request shedding to lower-priority variants), and pause non-essential background jobs (cache warmers).
  - burn_rate > 6x for 6h: enable circuit breaker on the route (reject new requests with 503 for lowest-priority tenants or routes), escalate to region-ejection staging (prepare traffic re-route).
  - burn_rate > 12x for 1h: regional ejection: shift traffic out of affected region(s) to healthy region(s) using priority routing; enable pinned fallbacks for enterprise customers only if opted-in.
- We define priority of actions so the system applies minimal customer-visible regression first (soft throttles, model substitution) before regional ejection.

Circuit breaker mapping and tuning guidance:
- Signals combined for tripping: short-window burn-rate (>6x), queue length > 80% of configured queue capacity, and queued_request_age P95 > 2s. All three must hold for 2 consecutive evaluation windows (30s each).
- When tripped:
  - Reject new requests for traffic slices with priority <= N (N depends on route: e.g., for public routes N=20; for enterprise N=100).
  - Emit event to ops bus and create a remediation runbook link via incident manager.
  - Auto-attempt re-enable at 1/2/4/8 minute backoffs if burn rate falls below 1.2x.

Regional fallback bands (new concept):
- A "fallback band" is an ordered list of compatible model variants + a capacity reservation plan used when a primary region degrades. Each band has: name, variant-order, capacity-reserve-percent, quality-degradation-allowance.
- Example band for /v1/generate (latency-sensitive):
  - Band-A (primary): [gptx-1.4fp16], reserve 80% capacity, quality-degradation 0%
  - Band-B (fallback-low-latency): [gptx-1.3-q8_0], reserve 10% capacity, quality-degradation <= 3%
  - Band-C (cost-shedding): [gptx-1.2-q4], reserve 10% capacity, quality-degradation <= 7%
- Ordering guarantees that during overload we first spill to Band-B variants (if compatible) before ejecting region or rejecting.

Routing and rollout orchestration:
- Smart router consults: route SLO targets, current burn-rate, regional capacity, and customer tier. It uses the following decision tree:
  1) If route SLO is currently OK and capacity available -> normal routing.
  2) If SLO breaching but burn_rate < 3x -> apply Band-B substitution locally.
  3) If burn_rate between 3x and 6x -> soft throttle low-priority tenants (token-based throttle) and expand Band-B usage.
  4) If burn_rate > 6x and region health is degraded -> region-ejection according to pre-set evacuation plan (move up to X% traffic per minute to target regions).

Testing and verification plan:
- Load test harness scenarios: synthetic spike (2x traffic for 10m), slow-node failure (increase first_token latency 3x), network partition (5% packet loss). Each scenario validated across:
  - SLI response (SLI metrics show expected burn pattern).
  - Router decision correctness (fallthrough uses Band-B, then ejection as configured).
- Test artifacts: load test pipeline PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2981
- Dashboards: SLI overview (https://dashboards.redwood.ai/slo/overview), per-route fallback band health (https://dashboards.redwood.ai/fallback-bands).

Operational runbook excerpts (what on-call does):
- Pager -> check SLO dashboard and fallback-band usage.
- If circuit-breaker tripped: confirm whether queue/backpressure or external region issue. If queue-driven, reduce ingress via WAF rule and scale serving pool (if autoscale available).
- If region-ejection started: coordinate with traffic-team to confirm target region capacity and activate customer pin overrides for enterprise customers.

Decisions made so far (meeting notes 2026-03-12):
- Agreed to standardize on P95 and P99 latency SLIs as primary latency indicators. (Decision by: Jonah Kim, Emily Chen, Marco Ruiz)
- Adopted "fallback band" construct rather than ad-hoc variant lists to make routing deterministic.
- Circuit-breaker requires combinational signals to reduce false positives.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Quality SLI actionability: Do we auto-fallback when quality SLI drops but latency/availability ok? (Risk: silent quality regressions). Proposal: only use quality SLI for rollout gating and alerts, not automated failover initially.
- Tenant priorities: how granular should priority slices be? Current prototype uses integer priority 0-255. Need a mapping to billing/tiering product metadata.

Next steps / action items:
- ENG: implement PromQL-based SLI exports for the 3 canonical SLIs across top 20 routes (owner: Marco, ETA 2026-03-20).
- PM: finalize priority-to-product mapping and publish in product policy doc (owner: Emily Chen, ETA 2026-03-18).
- SRE: run 3 scheduled load tests against Band-B substitution path and report results (owner: Jonah Kim, ETA 2026-03-24).
- Security: validate region-ejection audit logs meet compliance requirements (owner: Priya Nair, ETA 2026-03-28).

Related artifacts:
- Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/12345/SLO+Declaration+and+Fallback+Bands
- Load test PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2981
- Incident runbook draft: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/fallback-band-runbook-v0.pdf

Acceptance criteria:
- SLIs exported and visible in SLO service for the top 20 routes.
- Router respects fallback band ordering during synthetic test scenarios.
- Circuit-breaker triggers and recovers according to the mapped thresholds in two separate test runs.
- Documentation published and reviewed by PM, SRE, and Security.
